## Triage — task 10200 (verified 2026-11-05 at current main `882cb5d63e357438c13729aacb570f0a31842b08`)

**Verdict: #5797 is a valid, actionable design ticket. Keep it open; no implementation follow-up is needed now.**

- Current main has no latency-budget decision or implementation, and #5797 has no linked PR. Parent #5671 remains open.
- Keep scope to per-fallback-tier budgets for interactive use vs. bulk sync, plus a reproducible measurement/acceptance plan: proxy setup/TLS overhead, broker hop/framing, head-of-line blocking/multiplexing, keepalive/idle timeouts, and reconnect/resumption. Preserve #5671’s fallback ordering and E2E boundary; record the selected shape, alternatives, and implementation invariants as the issue requires.
- The completed #5791 decision record is merged as #6234 and explicitly assigns transport deadlines, the overall negotiation budget, and related timing values to this latency design. The completed #5794 record is merged as #6260; it says Workers may fit interactive and ordinary sync but not bulk throughput, and leaves HTTPS polling as a possible last-ditch tier. These decisions make #5797 necessary rather than superseded.
- **Ordering:** proceed now using #5791/#5794 as settled inputs. Work can run alongside #5792 (broker protocol/framing), #5793 (discovery), #5795 (trust/authorization), and #5796 (CONNECT traversal). State assumptions/provisional values where those unresolved mechanics affect measurements, then reconcile the final thresholds and fixtures with those design records—especially CONNECT, broker-hop, and multiplexing costs. #5796 is blocked; #5797 is not blocked from doing its design work.

The ticket itself is the design work item; implementation timing remains a separate decision as its body says.
